text: The conversations were friendly and exhaustive, and Mr. Kemp took the opportunity of making it quite clear that the Hongkong Government would not pay strike pay or compensation for non-reinstatement of strikers, nor would it countenance any such payment.

Brussels, April 16.
The International Miners Federation unanimously adopted a resolution declaring that the only way of emerging from an international coal crisis was to examine the International system of production and distribution.

label: text
text: It affirmed its complete solidarity with the British miners in the present dispute, and expressed its readiness, in the event of trouble, to take measures to prevent the exportation of coal to Great Britain.

label: text
text: In the event of an international strike, it would recommend that it be not discontinued before the National Associations are satisfied that there sufficient grounds for resuming work found in all countries involved in the conflict. The Federation would act as a Strike Committee for all countries.

As reported in Thursday's "China Mail," the Hongkong Tenants' Protective Association proposes to present a public petition to the Government, with regard to the notice to discontinue the present Rents Restriction Ordinance as from June 30, 1926.
Interviewed by a reporter yesterday, Mr. Wong Kam-ying (chairman of the Association) is quoted as having indicated that certain suggestions will be put forward before tomorrow's meeting.

label: text
text: In view of the bad trade conditions prevailing, one argument is that both residents and shopkeepers will find it very difficult to pay any additional rent during the boycott.

label: text
text: The main proposals are, that subject to the boycott continuing at any rate, the Ordinance be retained; or that landlords of houses at present under restriction be only allowed to raise rentals in accordance with a scale (to be fixed).

label: text
text: Failure to state specific damages led to judgment only for a nominal amount in the Supreme Court this morning, the case concerning an uncompleted house at 91 Shanghai Street, Yaumati.

label: text
text:
When the case had, originally been heard, Ng Iu, partner in the Tsau Loong firm (defendants) was allowed out of prison (where he was serving a term for debt), but the Chief Justice ruled his evidence out on account of his not having filed a statement of defence.
The Tai Tung-lim firm were plaintiffs.

label: text
text: Dealing with the evidence given on behalf of Tai Tung-lim. His Lordship said that the agreement had been made to complete the house by May 17, 1925. It had not in fact been completed on May 25 when all work was ceased by the defendants.

label: text
text: In spite of the agreement being that $10 was to be paid by the contractors for every day over the agreed time, no specific claim for specific damages had been put forward by the plaintiffs. His Lordship therefore held that plaintiff was only entitled to recover such damages as he could prove he had suffered by defendant's breach of the agreement.

label: text
text:
Plaintiff had stated that as defendants had started the work, the rules of the Contractors' Union forbade him to get anyone else to complete the work. But all that remained to be done was the cement concreting of the ground floor and work on windows. As plaintiff had only paid defendants $6,600 out of a total of $7,950, he would not appear to have suffered very much, said His Lordship, Certainly, plaintiff had given no evidence of damage incurred by him for which the defendants could be held responsible.
His Lordship therefore gave judgment for a nominal sum only, $10, without costs.
